To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a risk model for patients with AML older than 60 can be established that allows further stratification into 4 prognostically distinct groups.
we developed a novel prognostic score that allows the subdivision of patients with intermediate risk into 2 prognos-tic groups with a 3-year OS of 30% versus 10.6%.
a prognostic model based on karyotype, NPM1 mutational status, age, WBC, LDH, and CD34 was developed that allows the subdivision of the intermediate-risk group into 2 prognos-tic subgroups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a risk score for elderly patients with acute leukemia.
the analysis of prognostically relevant factors in elderly patients with AML and the development of a risk-adapted therapeutic strategy.
the identification of prognostic markers in elderly patients with AML and the development of a prognostic model that can be applied in the daily routine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AML96 trial was not able to demonstrate that a cytarabine- and idarubicin-based induction regimen followed by 1 course of consolidation is superior to a standard 3 + 3 regimen in terms of survival in elderly patients with AML.
the AML96 trial was a landmark trial for elderly patients with AML and that the AMLSG has been able to identify prognostic factors in this patient group.
age, karyotype, NPM1 status, and CD34 status are important prognostic factors in elderly patients with AML.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk model allows further subdivision of patients with an unfavorable prognosis into 2 prognoses.
this model is able to predict outcome for elderly patients with acute leukemia and can be used to guide therapy.
the AML96 risk model is an independent prognostic model for elderly patients with acute leukemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified 4 risk groups that allow the development of a risk-adapted therapeutic strategy in patients with acute leukemias.
the risk of death in elderly patients with AML is not uniform.
the AML96 trial provides the largest prospective study of patients older than 60 with acute myelogenous leukemia.
